title: Windowed admission and KV fallback policy for hot QPS
creator: Liam Chen
description: High-QPS workloads are exposing a failure mode where continuous batching increases latency variance and triggers out-of-memory GPU reclaiming when hot KV entries grow unexpectedly. This ticket implements a windowed admission controller that uses short-term windowed headroom estimates, an exponential backoff admission ramp, and a deterministic KV-fallback policy that gracefully sheds KV cache residency for low-value prefixes. Goals: 1) keep p99 latency <= 150ms for text-generation endpoints under sustained 4k QPS spikes, 2) avoid OOM-triggered preemption events on G4/G5 pools, and 3) provide telemetry to validate microbatch size distribution and KV hotness shifts.
acceptance_criteria: New admission controller deployed behind feature flag that enforces a sliding 1s window headroom estimate and admission rate cap
Under synthetic 4k QPS workload, p99 token latency remains <= 150ms and OOM events are zero in 30m run
KV-fallback policy evicts low-reuse prefixes within 200ms of crossing hotness threshold and preserves high-reuse keys
Console dashboard shows microbatch size histogram, headroom metric, KV-hotness heatmap and admission rejections with reasons
Automated Canary: two-minute failover to secondary model variant without capacity increase passes and rollback works
work_items: Design sliding-window headroom estimator (1s, 5s aggregations) and validate against historical QPS traces
Implement admission controller hook in request ingress to enforce window caps and exponential ramping
Add KV-fallback policy that tags prefixes by reuse score and provides eviction hints to KV manager
Integrate GPU memory probe metrics into headroom estimator and add soft-failure path that rejects non-priority requests
End-to-end tests: create synthetic harness to simulate bursty high-QPS and continuous sustained load
Dashboard cards and alerting thresholds in Console for p95/p99 latency, eviction rate, headroom, and admission rejections
Performance review and runbook updates for on-call when admission rejections exceed threshold

decisions: Use sliding 1s window for headroom estimate with a complementary 5s smoother to reduce oscillation
Admission ramp uses exponential backoff with base 1.5 per second when headroom decreases; ramp-down is linear to avoid sudden full-accept states
KV fallback is deterministic (score threshold) instead of purely LRU to prioritize high-value prefixes for retention
Soft-failure path rejects low-priority non-interactive requests first (embeddings/long-running batch jobs) before evicting KV entries
Feature flag rollout to 10% of traffic first, then 50%, then 100% pending SLO checks
tradeoffs: Responsiveness vs stability: 1s window improves reaction to sharp surges but increases sensitivity to transient noise; mitigated with 5s smoother
Deterministic eviction preserves important prefixes but may cause temporary fairness issues across tenants with similar prefix patterns
Rejecting low-priority requests reduces OOM risk but increases error rates for non-critical workloads; documented in console and tenant-facing notes
Extra instrumentation increases metric cardinality and cost but is necessary to validate correctness under production traffic
